lineage.strategy: Use the newly changed Palantir partnership input to separate distribution-channel evidence from contracted economics and prevent preferred-partner language from being treated as backlog.

observedWeaknesses.observation: Palantir named Nebius its preferred sovereign-AI infrastructure partner, but the announcement did not disclose committed contract value, customer conversion, deployment volume or economics.
observedWeaknesses.whyItMatters: Preferred-partner status expands distribution optionality but is not equivalent to contracted backlog or realized revenue.

risks.risk: Valuing the partnership as committed demand would inflate confidence because conversion, timing, margins and customer uptake remain undisclosed.

falsifiers.condition: Subsequent source-addressed disclosures show committed customer deployments, measurable revenue contribution and durable economics through the Palantir channel.

improvementPaths: Track disclosed customer deployments, contract value, utilization, margins and realized revenue through the partnership.

unknowns.unknown: Revenue contribution, deployment timing, margins and customer uptake remain undisclosed.

recommendation: Use as source-addressed backlog/TAM-confidence and execution-risk support without assigning Alpha's numeric risk or score.
